summary: David Kopf was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Chicago from around 1960 to 1965 and held a post at the University of Minnesota from circa 1967 to 1997.
David L. Gosling is a religious studies and Indology scholar. He held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall, Cambridge in 1992, and was affiliated with the University of Cambridge as attested in 2001.

David L. Haberman is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Colorado from 1970 to 1974. He held posts at the University of Arizona (~1989–1993) and Indiana University (around 1993).

David L. McMahan works in Buddhist and religious studies and taught at the University of Vermont and UC Santa Barbara. At Franklin & Marshall College, he was Assistant Professor of Religious Studies (attested 2002) and Professor (attested 2013).

David Llewellyn Snellgrove specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Southampton and Cambridge under D. R. Shackleton Bailey, H. W. Bailey, Walter Simon, and Giuseppe Tucci, he taught at SOAS University of London from 1950 to 1982.

David Ludden is a historian and Indologist who studied at Yale and the University of Pennsylvania. He held posts at the University of Virginia, the University of Pennsylvania (1981–2008), BRAC University (2005), and New York University (2007).

David M. DiValerio is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at SIT and earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Kurtis R. Schaeffer; he held a post at UW-Milwaukee (attested 2015).

David M. Knipe is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who held faculty positions at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, serving as Professor (attested 1975, 1998–2001) and South Asian Studies Professor and Chair of Religious Studies (attested 1989).

David Matsumoto is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies, including serving as its Director as attested in 2004, with his affiliation further attested in 2013.
David N. Keightley was a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology. He held a post as professor at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 1985 and 1999).

David N. Lorenzen is a historian, Indologist, and religious studies scholar. He studied at Wesleyan, SOAS, and ANU under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and Johannes Gijsbertus de Casparis, later serving as professor at El Colegio de México (1970–2010; emeritus 2019).

David Ownby is a scholar of sinology, history, and religious studies. After studying at Vanderbilt and Harvard, he taught at Southern Methodist University (~1990–1993) and served as Professor of History at the Université de Montréal (1994–2023).

David P. Chandler is a historian who studied at Harvard, Yale, and the University of Michigan. He held posts at Johns Hopkins, Cornell, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and Monash University (~1972–1997).

David P. Jackson is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his BA, MA, and PhD at the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg. He was a professor at the University of Hamburg from 1992 to 2007.
David Patt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the supervision of Geshe Lhundub Sopa, attested in 1993.

David Pingree was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Otto Neugebauer, he held posts at Harvard, the University of Chicago (1963–1971), and Brown University as professor from 1971.

David R. Kinsley was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Drew University, Union Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (~1964–1970). He held a post at McMaster University from 1969 to 2000.

David R. Loy is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned degrees from Carleton, King's College London, Hawaiʻi, and the National University of Singapore, later teaching at NUS (1978–1984), Bunkyo University (1990–2006), and Xavier University (~2006–2010).

David Ralph Quinter is a Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Colorado and Stanford University under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, later joining the University of Alberta (attested 2019).
David Ruddell was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Laval University and served as Secretary at Fort William College.
